title: Paul Magnier takes stage one Giro d’Italia pink jersey after huge crash in final 600m
content:
French sprinter Paul Magnier took the biggest victory of his promising professional career to earn the pink jersey after stage one of the Giro d’Italia.

With this year’s Grande Partenza taking place in Bulgaria, the end of the 147km stage in Burgos was marred by a huge crash involving several of the top sprint favourites with 600m remaining.

Just ten riders remained to contest the sprint, with Magnier of Soudal-Quickstep positioning himself perfectly in second-wheel before bursting around the in-form Tobias Lund Andresen to earn the pink jersey.

The win makes Magnier, 22, the youngest Frenchman to win a stage at a Grand Tour since Dominique Gaigne in 1983. Having taken 14 victories last season, the second-most behind Tadej Pogacar, Magnier entered his second Grand Tour with genuine designs on the ciclamino jersey awarded to the Giro’s top sprinter.

“I was really excited for the finale,” Magnier said in his post-race press conference. “Everyone was really fresh. The narrow road for the finale was tricky so we got in a good position. And then I could finish it off.”

Magnier’s ciclamino contenders Kaden Groves (Alpecin-Premier Tech) and Dylan Groenewegen (Unibet Rose Rockets) were both involved in the crash, with neither team having yet confirmed the extent of either rider’s injuries. Groenewegen appeared to have suffered a wrist injury, though both riders finished the stage.

No general classification (GC) favourites, such as Jonas Vingegaard or Giulio Pellizzari, went down in the crash, though they were held up behind. All riders received the same time (outside of bonuses) due to the crash taking place in the final five kilometres.

“It was a real narrow road at the end, (and) my front wheel just got clipped,” said Uno-X sprinter Erlend Blikra, the first rider to go down in the crash. “I don’t know if it was anyone’s mistake, but I was the first guy down and that’s not great. I have a lot of wounds on my back, so it’s going to be some long weeks now, unable to sleep how I want to.”

Tomorrow’s 221km stage is a hilly day from Burgas to Veliko Tarnovo featuring two mid-length climbs halfway through the stage, after which the pink jersey is expected to change hands once more.
